notes:
CIRCUIT: a single-loop AC ladder. A top rail at y~380 runs from x~188 to x~870 with two series elements sitting IN it - the V-AC source 9sin(5t+80)V at x~490 and the 63kohm resistor at x~727 - so the top rail is three separate nodes. A bottom rail at y~620 runs the whole width and is the common return; the GND symbol hangs below it at x~495. Four shunt branches drop from top to bottom: L 60mH (x~205), L 6H (x~361), C 62F (x~614) and the I-AC source 4sin(t)A (x~866) at the right-hand end.

NET MAP (4 nets):
  n1 = top rail, left segment (x 188..438): corner down to L#2 top lead (193,427), T at S5 down to L#3 top lead (350,435), on right to the V-AC left terminal (438,387). Terminals 0.0, 2.0, 3.0.
  n2 = top rail, middle segment (x 541..666): V-AC right terminal (541,391), T at S6 (610,394) down to the capacitor's upper plate lead (613,473), on right to the resistor's left lead (666,394). Terminals 0.1, 1.0, 5.0.
  n3 = top rail, right segment (x 789..870) plus the drop at the right edge: resistor right lead (789,406) right and down to I-AC top (850,468). Terminals 1.1, 4.0.
  0  = the bottom rail y~620 from x~205 to x~870 plus the GND stub. Terminals 2.1 (L 60mH bottom, 205,549), 3.1 (L 6H bottom, 362,560), 5.1 (capacitor lower plate lead, 613,528), 4.1 (I-AC bottom, 868,576), 6.0 (GND, 495,626).

SITE DECISIONS:
  S5 (348,387) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T at 5x and in the pixels: the 6H inductor's upper lead ends on the top rail, no dot, no hop, nothing passes through. Read otherwise the inductor's top would be a one-terminal net.
  S6 (610,394) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the capacitor's upper lead ends on the middle top-rail segment. (This site only became critical after the capacitor port fix below; before that the capacitor's t0 sat on label ink.) The other reading strands the capacitor.
  S14 (616,620) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the capacitor's lower lead ends on the bottom rail.
  S15 (359,622) deg3 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the 6H inductor's lower lead ends on the bottom rail.
  S16 (495,622) deg4 CRITICAL -> JUNCTION. The GND symbol's stem meets the bottom rail here (the extra degree comes from the rail being split either side plus the short stub into the GND box). Any other reading would leave the whole circuit without a ground reference and put GND on a net of its own.
  There are no ambiguous X crossings anywhere on this sheet - every wire meeting is a plain T or a corner. All the remaining sites (S0-S3, S7-S12) are strokes of the handwritten values '63kohm', '60mH', '6H', '62F', '4sint A' brushing a component box; left at their defaults and after the port fixes none of them carries a terminal.

PORT / TERMINAL FIXES (both are the classic 'terminal landed on the value label' error, each showing up as a one-terminal net):
  R#1: t1 was on port p5 @ (785,372), a 2 px fragment of the handwritten 'ohm' in '63kohm' sitting on top of the resistor box. Repointed to p6 @ (789,406), the real right-hand lead (a 125 px wire that runs right and down to the I-AC source's top terminal at (850,468)). t0 kept on p0 @ (666,394). Without this, n3 held only the resistor's own terminal and the I-AC top was a separate one-terminal net n4.
  C#5: t0 was on port p2 @ (572,488), a stroke of the handwritten '62F' touching the left edge of the capacitor box. Repointed to p1 @ (613,473), the real upper-plate lead going up to the top rail at S6. t1 kept on p0 @ (613,528), the lower-plate lead down to the bottom rail. Without this the capacitor's upper terminal was the one-terminal net n5.
  V-AC#0's spare port p2 @ (487,353) is the handwritten '9 sin(5t+80)V' label touching the top of the source circle; t0/t1 already pointed at the real left and right leads, so it was left alone. Same for I-AC#4's spare port p1 @ (812,542), which is the 'A' of '4 sin t A'.

RESULT: 7 components, 4 nets, ERC clean. No class looks wrong (two inductors, one capacitor, one resistor, a sine-source circle with no arrow = V-AC, a sine-source circle with a down arrow = I-AC, one GND). Nothing left unresolved.
